name: Avicii
description:
'''Tim Bergling'''{{efn|{{IPA|sv|ˈtɪmː ˈbæ̂rjlɪŋ|-|sv-Tim Bergling.ogg|small=no}}.}} (8 September 1989 – 20 April 2018), known professionally as '''Avicii''',{{efn|Pronounced {{IPAc-en|ə|ˈ|v|iː|tʃ|i}} {{respell|ə|VEE|chee}} in English, {{IPA|sv|aˈvɪ̌tːɕɪ|}} in Swedish}} was a Swedish [[DJ]], remixer, and [[record producer]]. His music consisted primarily of [[Pop music|pop]]-oriented [[house music]], often blended with other genres such as [[Folk music|folk]], [[Country music|country]], [[Bluegrass music|bluegrass]], [[Soul music|soul]], and [[blues]]. He is considered one of the most popular and successful [[electronic dance music]] (EDM) artists of all time and is credited with "leading EDM into the mainstream".

Avicii began posting remixes on [[Internet forum]]s when he was 16, and in May 2007, he was signed to the Dejfitts Plays record label. After winning a [[BBC Radio 1]] competition in 2008, he signed a [[talent management]] agreement with [[Arash Pournouri]]. "[[Levels (Avicii song)|Levels]]" (2011) was his first entry on the [[Billboard Hot 100 |''Billboard'' Hot 100]]. His debut studio album, ''[[True (Avicii album)|True]]'' (2013) peaked in the top 10 in more than 15 countries and topped international charts. The lead single, "[[Wake Me Up (Avicii song)|Wake Me Up]]", became a [[List of Spotify streaming records|most-streamed song on Spotify]]. Both his album [[Stories (Avicii album)|''Stories'']] (2015) and the [[extended play]] (EP) ''[[Avīci (01)]]'' (2017) reached number one on the Swedish [[Sverigetopplistan]] chart. His third and final album, ''[[Tim (Avicii album)|Tim]]'' (2019), was released posthumously and reached number one on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Top Dance Albums]] chart.

Avicii, a self-described shy person, suffered from [[anxiety]] and [[Depression (mood)|depression]] and used alcohol as a [[coping]] mechanism. In 2012, Avicii was hospitalized for 11 days in [[New York City]] with [[acute pancreatitis]] caused by [[alcoholism]]. Between 2012 and 2014, to treat pain from the pancreatitis, Avicii was prescribed [[opioid]]s such as [[OxyContin]] and [[Vicodin]], to which he developed an [[addiction]]. He ignored the advice of doctors, leading to a ruptured appendix and, in March 2014, he underwent surgery to remove his [[Appendix (anatomy)|appendix]] and [[gallbladder]]. He entered a [[drug rehabilitation]] facility in 2015 after his closest friends and family organized an [[Intervention (counseling)|intervention]] in Ibiza. Due to these health issues, Avicii announced his retirement from touring in March 2016. He experienced significant anxiety over the possibility of disappointing his fans and in 2018, while on vacation in [[Muscat]], Oman, Avicii committed [[suicide]] at the age of 28, using a broken wine bottle to cause "massive bleeding".

Avicii's accolades included four [[MTV Europe Music Awards]], two [[International Dance Music Awards]], one [[American Music Award]], and one [[Billboard Music Award]]. He was nominated for a [[Grammy Award|Grammy]] for his work on "[[Sunshine (David Guetta song)|Sunshine]]" with [[David Guetta]] in 2012 and "Levels" in 2013. His nightly fees were estimated at $250,000 or higher.
